newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks soar 3.05 pct on rising yen vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks soar 3.05 pct on rising yen vs dollar.

text.p: South Korean stocks soared in Thursday afternoon trading on hopes that the strength of the Japanese yen versus the U.S. dollar could help boost earnings by domestic companies, brokers said.
The composite stock index rose 3.05 percent, or 20.88 points, to 704.74 at 0522 GMT.
"The yen's rise is boosting major manufacturing stocks, especially shipbuilding and other heavy-industrial sectors," said Koh Soon-shik of LG Securities.

The yen rose to as high as 116.20 yen to the dollar in Tokyo trading at 0300 GMT. A stronger yen would make South Korean exports more competitive in world markets as Seoul and Tokyo compete in similar products.
The sub-index for the transportation equipment manufacturers, including vehicle makers, gained 4.91 percent to 565.65 and that for machinery makers rose 4.40 percent to 614.39.
Blue chips also gained across the board.
Samsung Electronics gained 1,700 won to 63,500 and POSCO added 900 won to 54,600.
Investors shrugged off a political scandal involving the president's second son.
President Kim Young-sam's son, Hyun-chul, is due to arrive at the prosecutor's office in the afternoon for questioning over allegations that he took bribes from companies.
Samlip General Foods Co said early on Thursday it planned to file for court receivership due to serious financial problems. Trading in the stock has been suspended.
